trustmart.title: TrustMart: know what you are comparing

scenes.title: Start with the real problem
scenes.label: ACTUAL INTERFACE CAPTURE
scenes.text: In Lahore's electronics markets, two similar-looking parts may have very different quality, warranties, and prices. TrustMart helps a buyer inspect those differences before deciding.

scenes.title: Compare like with like
scenes.label: EXPLANATORY DIAGRAM
scenes.text: First, describe the component precisely. A phone model, component type, quality grade, and warranty define the comparison group. A cheaper but different part is not automatically a better offer.

scenes.title: Decide which offers qualify
scenes.label: FICTIONAL TEACHING PRICES
scenes.text: The price engine keeps approved offers from verified suppliers, with stock available and timestamps no older than seven days. A revoked, stale, or unavailable offer cannot influence this calculation.

scenes.title: Explain the calculation
scenes.label: FICTIONAL TEACHING PRICES
scenes.text: With five or more eligible offers, it removes twenty percent from each end of the sorted prices, then averages the remaining values. Smaller samples use the ordinary mean and show low confidence.

scenes.title: Follow the shop record
scenes.label: EXPLANATORY DIAGRAM
scenes.text: A camera scan or manual Shop I D resolves through the backend to the current supplier record. Verified describes that record. It does not prove every product is authentic or guarantee compensation.

scenes.title: Build trust through evidence
scenes.label: ACTUAL INTERFACE CAPTURE
scenes.text: Customers can inspect disclosures, supplier status, and report a problem. Suppliers and administrators have separate permissions. This demo uses fictional shops and sample prices, making its limits visible alongside its features.

scenes.title: Begin with the whole journey
scenes.label: ACTUAL INTERFACE CAPTURE
scenes.text: A flight price is only one part of a trip. Travel Estimator brings transport, accommodation, daily spending, extras, and a contingency into one explained planning budget.

scenes.title: Keep the source visible
scenes.label: EXPLANATORY DIAGRAM
scenes.text: Base costs are illustrative estimates. Configured providers can return dated flight quotes and venue information. The interface distinguishes those sources instead of presenting every number as a current booking price.

scenes.title: Protect the selected quote
scenes.label: EXPLANATORY DIAGRAM
scenes.text: Before applying a flight, the server checks who selected it, the route, travel dates, and party size. A selection older than fifteen minutes must be refreshed. The browser cannot simply invent verified quote metadata.

scenes.title: Make the price basis explicit
scenes.label: ILLUSTRATIVE CALCULATION
scenes.text: For example, seven hundred dollars at an assumed rate of two hundred eighty Pakistani rupees becomes one hundred ninety-six thousand rupees for a group. If it is a per-person fare, two travellers double that flight amount.

scenes.title: Replace once, then recalculate
scenes.label: ILLUSTRATIVE CALCULATION
scenes.text: The selected flight replaces the sample transport line once. Other costs remain. The subtotal and contingency are recalculated, while baggage, transfers, and seller fees still need separate confirmation.

scenes.title: Be honest when data is missing
scenes.label: ACTUAL INTERFACE CAPTURE
scenes.text: A provider may return no photos, no usable offers, or a quota error. The app explains that result. It does not replace missing live data with invented bargains. A saved plan is a snapshot, not a reservation.

scenes.title: An easy button, a harder problem
scenes.label: ACTUAL INTERFACE CAPTURE
scenes.text: Booking an appointment looks like a simple click. But two people may request the same doctor and time. A reliable system must make one correct decision, even when both screens looked available.

scenes.title: Check authority before writing
scenes.label: EXPLANATORY DIAGRAM
scenes.text: CareIndex checks the request origin and session first. Staff need the right permission. A patient account is tied to its own fictional profile, so changing a browser field cannot book for an unrelated patient.

scenes.title: Put the check inside the transaction
scenes.label: TEACHING SIMULATION
scenes.text: The booking path begins an immediate SQLite transaction before checking availability. SQLite serialises writers. This prevents two independent check-then-write sequences from both treating the same slot as free.

scenes.title: Keep the invariant in the database
scenes.label: TEACHING SIMULATION
scenes.text: A partial unique index allows only one scheduled booking for a doctor, date, and time. The application also checks working hours and existing reservations. The database rule remains a final protection.

scenes.title: Commit the complete change
scenes.label: TEACHING SIMULATION
scenes.text: The appointment and its invoice are created inside the same transaction. Both commit together. If something fails, the transaction rolls back. A competing request receives a controlled conflict instead of a second reservation.

scenes.title: Understand what the demo proves
scenes.label: ACTUAL INTERFACE CAPTURE
scenes.text: The engineering lab explains database behaviour and separate algorithms, including A V L rotations. It does not claim that a teaching tree replaces SQLite indexing. All patients are fictional, and payments are simulated.

word-search.title: Word Search Studio: make every target achievable

scenes.title: A small game with real invariants
scenes.label: ACTUAL INTERFACE CAPTURE
scenes.text: Word Search Studio began as a C plus plus console game. The browser edition keeps its fifteen-by-fifteen board and difficulty rules, while adding accessible controls, automatic resume, and an explanation of the search.

scenes.title: Use a seed, not a mystery
scenes.label: EXPLANATORY DIAGRAM
scenes.text: A seeded random sequence makes the same puzzle reproducible for the same rules and generator version. Daily puzzles derive that seed from a shared U T C date, rather than storing a new random board for every visitor.

scenes.title: Place words before filler
scenes.label: ALGORITHM VISUALISATION
scenes.text: The generator tries bounded placements for each target. Matching letters may overlap. Only successfully placed words enter the target list. Random letters fill the empty cells afterwards, so listed targets remain achievable.

scenes.title: Validate the line
scenes.label: ALGORITHM VISUALISATION
scenes.text: Easy allows horizontal lines. Intermediate adds vertical lines, and hard adds diagonals. The selected cells must form a straight permitted path. Forward and reverse selections resolve to the same canonical target.

scenes.title: Reward a discovery once
scenes.label: ALGORITHM VISUALISATION
scenes.text: A newly found word earns ten points. Selecting it again earns nothing and costs no life. Classic mode penalises wrong attempts, while relaxed mode lets a student explore without that penalty.

scenes.title: Make the logic visible
scenes.label: ACTUAL INTERFACE CAPTURE
scenes.text: The algorithm view highlights candidate starts and directions until it finds a match. Tests check generation, permitted paths, reverse selection, and reproducibility. Personal records stay in the browser; they are not a verified global leaderboard.
